# Research Ethics Review — Applicant Conversation

Panel pre-meeting script. Used by the panel secretary before the committee sits.

## Notes for the secretary

Ask the Foundation questions of every applicant. Beyond that, **prioritise no more
than three** of the situational areas — the committee reads a focused conversation
far better than an exhaustive one, and a fourth area rarely changes a decision.
Where an area is clearly relevant but not among your three, note it for the
committee rather than covering it.

Two areas are covered **briefly** wherever they apply: Data management and
Dissemination. For these, one or two questions is sufficient — you are establishing
that the applicant has thought about it, not assessing the detail.

Consent and Vulnerable participants, where they apply, are covered **in full**.

## Foundation

1. In plain language, what are you trying to find out?
2. Who are your participants, and how many?
3. How will you recruit them?
4. What is the single most sensitive thing you are asking of a participant?

## Situational area — Consent

Relevant where participants are individuals rather than institutions.

5. How will you explain the study to a participant before they agree?
6. How can a participant withdraw, and until what point?
7. What happens to data already collected if someone withdraws?
8. How will you record that consent was given?

## Situational area — Vulnerable participants

Relevant where any participant may lack capacity, is under eighteen, or is in a
dependent relationship with a researcher.

9. Which participants might be considered vulnerable, and why?
10. Who else will be involved in the consent process?
11. What safeguards are in place during data collection?
12. How would you recognise distress, and what would you do?

## Situational area — Data management

Relevant where any personal data is collected.

13. Where will the data live, and who can reach it?
14. When will identifiers be removed or destroyed?

## Situational area — Deception or partial disclosure

Relevant where participants will not be told the full purpose in advance.

15. What exactly will participants not be told, and why is it necessary?
16. How and when will they be debriefed?
17. What will you do if a participant objects after debriefing?

## Situational area — Overseas fieldwork

Relevant where data collection happens outside the United Kingdom.

18. What local approvals are required, and what is their status?
19. How does local law differ on consent or data?
20. What is your withdrawal plan if conditions deteriorate?

## Situational area — Dissemination

Relevant where findings will be published in any form.

21. How will you prevent participants being identified in outputs?

## Situational area — Conflict of interest

Relevant where any researcher has a financial or personal interest in the outcome.

22. What is the interest, and who holds it?
23. How will it be managed and declared?

## Closing

24. What part of this application do you expect the committee to challenge?
25. What have you changed since you first designed the study?
